name: Palau
snapshot: A small, US-aligned island nation that recognises Taiwan and has offered to host more US military facilities.
culture: Palau's Rock Islands, a UNESCO site, and Jellyfish Lake draw divers worldwide. Society is matrilineal, with women's councils holding traditional authority over land and titles. Visitors must sign the "Palau Pledge" in their passport, promising to protect the environment.
society: Tourism and US compact funding underpin the economy. Palau created one of the world's largest marine sanctuaries. Chinese tourist numbers fell after Beijing discouraged travel, seen as pressure over Taiwan. The US is building a radar system on the islands.
situation: Surangel Whipps Jr. won re-election in November 2024. He has urged a stronger US military presence and agreed in 2025 to take some third-country migrants deported from the US.
power: A presidential republic modelled on the US. The president is directly elected for four years, the legislature has a Senate and a House of Delegates, and a Council of Chiefs advises on custom.
